authors: Liang, C., Li, W., Dong, Y. & Fu, W.
title: Single domain generalization method for remote sensing image segmentation via category consistency on domain randomization
source: IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing 62, 1-16
relevance: Names our exact regime and gives it a literature: SINGLE domain generalization - train on ONE source domain, deploy to unseen domains, no target data at training time. That is 2020-labels-only deployed across 17 other acquisitions, and Search 23 concluded no published work covered it; this is the formalization we were missing. Its mechanism is domain randomization with a category-consistency constraint, which is the principled version of 'augment harder' and answers our consensus finding (a) directly. Peer-reviewed in TGRS - the strongest single match to our constraint found in this loop.

authors: Yaras, C., Kassaw, K., Huang, B., Bradbury, K. & Malof, J.M.
title: Randomized histogram matching: A simple augmentation for unsupervised domain adaptation in overhead imagery
relevance: Head-to-head evidence for OVERHEAD imagery specifically that randomized histogram matching - matching each training image to a randomly drawn reference histogram - is competitive with, and cleaner than, GAN-based style transfer, which introduces artifacts and blurred patterns. That is a direct verdict on the Phase 2 Search 5 question and a caution against the generative route (StandardGAN ID 30, diffusion ID 37): the simple method wins on our data type. Cheapest possible test of consensus finding (a) - it needs no new model, only a change to the augmentation pipeline, and it can be tried on the 2017 matched pair immediately.

title: Boosting domain generalization in remote sensing image segmentation via style mapping and general prototypical contrast
relevance: Top-venue treatment of RS segmentation domain generalization that separates STYLE (a lightweight style mapper built from statistical style prototypes) from CONTENT (prototypical contrast on categories) - the same amplitude-versus-semantics split arrived at from a third direction, after FDA (ID 136) and amplitude mixup (ID 139). Useful because it transfers style knowledge statistically rather than generatively, avoiding the artifact problem Yaras 2024 documents. Read alongside Liang 2024: one gives the regime, this gives the mechanism.
